parsed_output.analysis: The specification requires an explicit power-on entry to Human Driving Mode, a return to Human Driving Mode only from the autonomous final sub-state on human steering command / brake pressed, and a power-off transition to a final state. The PlantUML model implements a start transition without an event, adds a return transition from the operational sub-state, and uses the termination pseudo-state [*] for power-off instead of an explicit final state.

issues.issue: Power-on entry is not modelled with an event
issues.reason: Specification 3 says 'when power on, the system turn into human driving mode'. The model has an unlabeled start transition [*] -> HumanDrivingMode with no Power On trigger/event, so the required power-on condition is missing.

issues.issue: Return to Human Driving Mode is allowed from AutoOperationalState in addition to AutoFinalState
issues.reason: Specification 4 says transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final). The model also provides AutoOperationalState -> HumanDrivingMode on the same condition, introducing a transition that is not specified and should be restricted to the auto final sub-state only.
issues.where: AutoOperationalState -> HumanDrivingMode: human steering cmd, brake pressed

issues.issue: Power-off targets termination pseudo-state instead of a final state
issues.reason: Specification 5 says 'when power off, it will transit to final state'. The model transitions to the UML termination pseudo-state [*] on Power Off. No explicit named final state is used for the power-off destination, so the required final-state target is not conformant.
issues.where: HumanDrivingMode -> [*]: Power Off and AutonomousMode -> [*]: Power Off

system_prompt:
You are an experienced control-systems engineer reviewing a state machine model against the natural-language specification it was built from.

You are given two things, both complete and unmodified:
  1. The natural-language specification.
  2. A state machine model written in PlantUML.

Your task: identify the places where the model does not conform to the specification. Read the specification in full first, then read the model in full, then report what you find.

Report as many or as few issues as you actually find, and organize them however you judge best. For each issue, state what the non-conformance is, which part of the model it concerns, and why you consider it a non-conformance.

Write your findings in en-US. Return only the requested structured response.
user_prompt:
## Natural-language specification

1 The human driving mode is represented by a simple state. 2 The autonomous mode has sub-states and is represented by a sub machine state. 3. when power on, the system turn into human driving mode 4when front_distance > 10, auto transport to autonomous state 4. transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final) 5 when power off, it will transit to final state

## State machine model (PlantUML)

@startuml
[*] -> HumanDrivingMode
HumanDrivingMode: Human Driving Mode
HumanDrivingMode -> AutonomousMode: front_distance > 10
AutonomousMode: Autonomous Mode
state AutonomousMode {
[*] -> AutoInitialState
AutoInitialState: Initial State
AutoInitialState -> AutoOperationalState: Signal Transmission Succeeds
AutoOperationalState: Operational State
AutoOperationalState -> AutoFinalState: Mission Completed
AutoFinalState: Final State
AutoOperationalState -> HumanDrivingMode: human steering cmd, brake pressed
AutoFinalState -> HumanDrivingMode: human steering cmd, brake pressed
}
HumanDrivingMode -> [*]: Power Off
AutonomousMode -> [*]: Power Off
@enduml
